Subject: Vendor onboarding & payment method — PO vs card (post-demo follow-up)

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the demo with Michael and the infra team this morning. Couple quick follow-ups to help us map the commercial path:

- Procurement preference: did your AP team indicate whether they prefer paying via PO (net terms) or company card? We often see mid-market finance teams require a PO + vendor onboarding for new suppliers.
- Vendor onboarding: do you have a standard vendor packet we should complete? Happy to loop in legal/finance on our side.
- Marketplace interest: you mentioned Marketplace integrations during the call — is that something you'd prefer for procurement to avoid a vendor onboarding flow?

Next steps I suggest: if PO is required, we can send a vendor packet and SOW template and coordinate with your AP contact; if card is acceptable we can provision a short-term card-based pilot to speed the first integration.

I attached a short onboarding checklist we use (see attached). If you want, I can also introduce Rishi (our finance lead) to talk terms and invoicing cadence.

Thanks — let me know what works.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding & payment method — PO vs card (post-demo follow-up)

Hi Marissa —

Excited about what we saw — thanks for the clear walkthrough. Quick answers from AP/procurement:

- Payment method: Our AP prefers POs with net-30 for any new vendors over $10k/year. Cards are allowed for pilots under $5k, but require business-justification.
- Vendor onboarding: We do have a vendor packet and we will need a completed W9 + brief insurance certificate. I attached our W9 for your records and internal packet.
- Marketplace: We are open to Marketplace purchases (internal procurement loves that), but the marketplace listing process takes 4–6 weeks and needs vendor registration. If you're open to the marketplace, procurement will evaluate that as an option to streamline future renewals.

Next step for us: can you send the Redwood vendor packet + W9? If we decide to go PO route we'll create an internal PR and loop Legal. If we want a quick pilot to unblock dev, we can start with a card and then convert to a PO for production.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Caldwell
Senior Procurement Manager | FintechCo
sophie.caldwell@fintechco.com
